findings.evidence: dom-1440.json: 'Download CV' is an a with href '#contact'. It downloads nothing; it scrolls to the contact form.

findings.where: social links (hero and footer), brand link
findings.evidence: GitHub, LinkedIn and Twitter icon links have accessible names but all point to '#'; the 'AC' brand link also goes to '#'. Six focus stops that do nothing (focus.json stops 1, 9-11, 17-19).
findings.after: Real profile URLs, or remove the links. [DATA NEEDED: profile URLs]
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.4.4 Link Purpose; a control whose name promises a destination it does not reach.

findings.evidence: forms.json: the form has action null and method get; pressing 'Send Message' made one request and produced no new text, so a user gets no confirmation or error. Fields have visible labels, but placeholders ('John Doe', 'john@example.com') are example data and no field shows a required state or error message.
findings.before: <form method="get"> … no error or success region
findings.after: action pointing at a real endpoint; required + aria-invalid on failure, an error text tied with aria-describedby, and an aria-live="polite" status after send.
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 3.3.1 Error Identification, 3.3.3 Error Suggestion and 4.1.3 Status Messages.

findings.evidence: Project cards contain h3 titles but are not links and contain no links; a keyboard or screen-reader user (like anyone) has no way to open a project. focus.json goes straight from the hero to the form inputs.
findings.after:
[Project name]

with the card made clickable via the heading link.
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.1.1 Keyboard (functionality implied by hover-styled 'group' cards) and 1.3.1.

findings.evidence: nav and footer landmarks but no main (sweep) and no skip link; the hero and sections are not in a header/main. Six nav/brand stops precede the content.
findings.after:
Skip to content and
around the sections.

findings.evidence: The 'AC' circle, '</>' tile, palette tile and person-silhouette avatar are decorative; the 'AC' text inside the circle is read aloud as 'A C' a second time after the h1. Confirm they are aria-hidden.

strengths: Every input has a visible, programmatically associated label (names 'Name', 'Email', 'Subject', 'Message').
Icon-only social links carry accessible names (GitHub, LinkedIn, Twitter).

disputed: tag-pill contrast (e.g. #00d3f2 on #e5f7fb at 1.64:1) may also be shim colours, not the authored palette; re-run with the real Tailwind config before reporting
focus visibility and non-text contrast of inputs not judged for the same reason
